about.title: Orland Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Slip and fall accidents in Orland often happen where people least expect them — a wet floor at a store near South Street, a cracked walkway along Rt 32, or poor lighting in a parking lot off Walker Street. Glenn County's smaller-town layout means many falls occur on commercial or retail property, where owners have a legal duty to keep spaces reasonably safe. Under California law, you generally need to show the property owner knew, or should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why documenting the scene matters — photos of the spill, torn carpet, or broken step, plus witness names, can make a real difference later. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect injured Orland residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Fall

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help track down maintenance logs, prior complaint records, or incident history that establishes this.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Orland businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having nothing.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, a Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're partly responsible for not seeing a hazard, you may still recover a share of damages reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Orland?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit for injury claims. If the property involved is owned by a government or public entity, the deadline is much shorter and involves an early claim-filing requirement. It's worth talking to an attorney soon so you don't lose the option to pursue anything.

items.question: What if I fell but didn't take pictures at the time?
items.answer: It's not ideal, but it's not necessarily the end of your case. An attorney can help track down store surveillance footage, incident reports the business may have filed, or witness statements from people who saw the hazard. The sooner this happens after a fall in Orland, the better the chances that evidence still exists.

items.question: Does it matter that Orland is a small town with fewer big stores?
items.answer: Not really — the same premises liability rules apply whether the fall happened at a small local shop near Walker Street or a larger retailer. What matters is whether the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An independent attorney can look at the specific location and circumstances of your fall.
